title: Auth tests seed jobs directly into the server's SQLite job store
answers: how do I create jobs for a basic-auth server test
seed job rows for a FastAPI auth test without submitting over HTTP
build sqlite uri for test job store on windows and posix
create a legacy job with no creator in a test
body:
Seed jobs in auth tests by constructing mlflow/store/jobs/sqlalchemy_store.py:SqlAlchemyJobStore on the same SQLite file the fixture points the server at, then call create_job(name, params, creator=...).
HTTP submit would need job execution enabled plus an allowlisted job function in the auth fixture, and cannot produce a creator-less row, so it is avoided.
URI: use 'sqlite:////' plus the path for POSIX and 'sqlite://' plus the path on Windows, as in tests/server/auth/test_auth.py:test_job_search_only_returns_callers_jobs.
create_job commits on session exit, so rows are visible to the running server and its huey worker subprocess.
applies: Basic-auth FastAPI tests in tests/server/auth/ that need job rows with specific creators.
says: Job search results should only display background tasks created by the signed-in user.
Users are able to see background jobs submitted by other workspace members.
Legacy jobs created without an owner should not be exposed to unauthorized callers.
Filtering jobs in the dashboard should hide tasks belonging to other user accounts.
Make sure search queries return only the active user's queued and completed jobs.
search: In tests/server/auth/, basic-auth FastAPI tests seed job rows directly into SQLite using SqlAlchemyJobStore rather than submitting over HTTP. Tests construct mlflow/store/jobs/sqlalchemy_store.py:SqlAlchemyJobStore pointing to the fixture SQLite file via 'sqlite:////' on POSIX or 'sqlite://' on Windows, then call create_job(name, params, creator=...). This bypasses the need for job execution and allowlisted functions while allowing creator-less legacy rows, committing on session exit to remain visible to the server and huey worker subprocess.
